findings.description: deliver is now a coroutine function, but flush calls it without await. The coroutine object is always truthy, so the branch always takes the success path. No message is ever sent (the coroutine never runs, with a 'never awaited' warning), lines are deleted from the queue as if delivered, and failed is always empty. This is silent data loss of queued digests.
findings.title: Missing await on async deliver() makes every digest look delivered

findings.description: Once deliver is awaited, other coroutines may call add() during the send. After the await, `del lines[:sent]` is correct only if the list object is still the same. The iteration `for recipient in sorted(self._pending)` uses a snapshot, so it is safe. But `del self._pending[recipient]` could race with a concurrent flush that already removed the key, raising KeyError. Also, render() is computed from all lines, which may exceed MAX_LINES, while only `sent` lines are removed, which is fine. The race on concurrent flushes is the issue.
findings.suggestion: Use `self._pending.pop(recipient, None)` and guard against concurrent flushes, for example with an asyncio.Lock.
findings.title: Mutating the list and deleting the dict key across an await can lose lines or raise
